name: audit
title: Action history
summary: The tamper-evident action history: who did what, in which role, to which record, why, what changed (before and after), which approvals applied and the request id. Every module writes to it through record(); staff read it with filters and authorized exports; retention is a governed setting.
owns: Append-only action history entries (cannot be edited or deleted by anyone; only purged after retention)
Actor, actor roles at the time, action, module, target and related targets, reason, before/after (structured and human text), approval state, request id, IP
Approval state of each entry (not required / pending / approved / rejected …), kept current from access events without changing the entry
Search and filters (staff, role, target, action, category, approval state, date range) and per-record history for detail pages
Authorized exports of the action history (CSV, JSON lines; reason required and recorded), run as reports export jobs (dataset audit.admin.entries)
Retention setting with a legal minimum, purge job, and hash-chain integrity checks
Seller-visible history of actions on the seller's own account (seller staff changes, payout destination changes)
notOwns: Account security activity shown to customers (sign-ins, password changes): identity.security_events
Approval requests, limits and decisions: access (audit stores the request id and a projection of its state)
Record timelines shown to customers and sellers (order timeline, return progress): owning modules
Business reports and their exports: reports

publicApi.name: record
publicApi.desc: Append one entry. Call it inside the same transaction as the change (outbox once introduced), so a change is never saved without its history. Roles are resolved through access.rolesOf when the actor is staff and actorRoles is omitted.

publicApi.name: recordMany
publicApi.desc: Bulk actions (bulk catalog edit, payout run items) in one call

publicApi.name: historyOf
publicApi.signature: (targetType: string, targetId: string, limit?: int) => AuditEntry[]
publicApi.desc: Staff history for a record, embedded in other modules' admin detail responses (order, seller, payout)

publicApi.name: trailOf
publicApi.signature: (targetType: string, targetIds: string[], opts: { includeRelated?: bool, category?: string, page?: PageInput }) => Map<string, Page<AuditEntry>>
publicApi.desc: Batched, paged history per record for the Action history card on admin 360 views (order, seller, customer, payout run). includeRelated also matches entries where the record is one of relatedTargets. Newest first.

publicApi.name: searchEntries
publicApi.desc: The action history with filters, newest first (same as GET /entries)

publicApi.name: getEntry
publicApi.desc: One entry with before/after and approval

publicApi.name: exportRows
publicApi.signature: (dataset: string, filters: json, principal: identity.Principal, cursor?: string) => { rows: json[], nextCursor?: string }
publicApi.desc: Export rows for reports dataset audit.admin.entries (filters are AuditFilters; values are already redacted at record time)

tables.name: entries
tables.desc: Append-only: the repository only inserts entries and never updates or deletes them, except the retention purge (audit.purge-expired), which deletes the entries before the cut-off by their indexed at; the database user's role should allow no update or delete on audit.* but the purge's. hash = sha256(prev_hash || canonical row). search_words holds the lower-case words of the refs, labels, reason, names and action (the simple text search behind q).

columns.search_words: text[] (lower-case words of refs, labels, reason, names and action)

tables.name: entry_targets
tables.desc: Related targets for history lookups (an order item entry also appears under its order and seller). at is the entry's at, so the purge deletes a target row with its entry; written in the same transaction as the entry.

tables.name: approval_states
tables.desc: Projection of access approval requests referenced by entries; updated from access events, so entries stay immutable

tables.name: checkpoints
tables.desc: Signed chain checkpoints: written after each successful verification and before a purge, so verification continues across purged ranges and a rewritten chain is detected even if every hash was recomputed

stateMachines.name: Retention change
stateMachines.notes: Lengthening applies at once. Shortening needs Business Owner approval (action audit.retention.change) and never goes below minimumYears; the next purge uses the new value.

endpoints.desc: Newest first. Each item is complete (actor and role, action, target, reason, before → after, approval state), so the table and phone list render from one call.

endpoints.summary: One entry with evidence and approval history
Counts for the filter chips (pending second review, financial, enforcement, settings)
History of one record (order, seller, payout, product, setting…)
endpoints.desc: Includes entries where the record is a related target. Used for 'staff history with reasons' panels.

Records the reason in the action history, then creates an authorized export job through reports.requestExport (dataset audit.admin.entries, csv or jsonl). Poll GET /exports/{id} for the download link. Limited to reports.maxExportRows, read through settings (settings.get('reports.maxExportRows')) and checked against the matching entry count before the job is created.
Proxies reports.listExports for dataset audit.admin.entries: the caller's own jobs, or every requester's with audit.retention.manage.

endpoints.summary: Export status and a fresh download link
endpoints.desc: Proxies reports.getExport: only the requester may download, and each signed link is recorded.

endpoints.summary: Change how long history is kept
endpoints.desc: Lengthening applies now. Shortening is saved as pendingChange and sent to the Business Owner (approval action audit.retention.change): the normal 200 with pendingChange.approval (FORMAT.md, Approval responses); it applies when approved and is dropped when rejected, cancelled or expired. When access answers allowed for the caller, it applies at once. APPROVAL_REQUIRED (409, nothing saved) only while the access module is disabled, so no approval can be requested; FORBIDDEN when the caller may not even propose it. While a shortening waits, no other retention change is accepted (ILLEGAL_TRANSITION).
endpoints.approval: Approval action audit.retention.change. Shortening retention needs Business Owner approval

endpoints.summary: Changes made on this seller account
endpoints.desc: Seller member changes (staff, permissions, store details, payout destination) and staff actions marked visible to the seller. Staff names are not shown.

publishes.name: audit.retention.changed
publishes.when: The retention period changes (after approval when shortened)

publishes.name: audit.integrity.failed
publishes.when: The hash-chain check finds a broken link

consumes.name: access.approval.requested
consumes.does: Create or reset the approval_states row (pending, awaiting the eligible reviewers)

consumes.name: access.approval.partially_approved
consumes.does: Add the first approval to approval_states (still pending a second reviewer)

consumes.name: access.approval.returned
consumes.does: Mark the approval state returned with the comment

consumes.name: access.approval.decided
consumes.does: Set the final approval state and decision time; for audit.retention.change apply or drop the pending retention change

permissions.desc: Read the action history, its integrity status and the retention policy. Seeded to the Business Owner and the Platform Administrator (told about integrity failures, proposes retention changes); other roles (e.g. a Finance Manager or an auditor) get it through their role's permissions
Export action history (sensitive; every export is recorded)
Change the retention period (shortening still needs Business Owner approval). Seeded to the Business Owner and Platform Administrator roles
See changes made on the seller's own account (owner by default)

approvalActions.desc: Shorten the action-history retention period (never below the legal minimum; lengthening needs no approval)

jobs.name: audit.verify-chain
jobs.does: Verify the newest checkpoint's HMAC, recompute hashes from it; on success write a new signed checkpoint at the last seq; on a hash or signature mismatch publish audit.integrity.failed (Platform Administrator and Business Owner are notified)

jobs.name: audit.purge-expired
jobs.does: Write a signed checkpoint at the last entry before the cut-off (retainYears, never below minimumRetentionYears, at a market month start), then delete the entries before the cut-off that come before every kept entry in the chain, with their related targets (by the indexed at). Record the purge as an entry (removedEntries, checkpoint) so the chain still verifies

jobs.name: audit.prepare-partitions
jobs.does: Nothing to prepare on MongoDB (entries are one collection, not month partitions): kept under its name and schedule, and always succeeds

settings.desc: Years entries are kept (example value on the prototype)
Legal floor; changed only by configuration, not the API
Keys masked in before/after JSON at record time

EXPORT_TOO_LARGE.meaning: The filters match more than reports.maxExportRows; narrow the date range. details.matched, details.max.

BELOW_LEGAL_MINIMUM.meaning: Retention cannot be shorter than details.minimumYears.

notes: Material actions: every endpoint marked audited in any module calls audit.record (the kernel provides a helper that fills actor, roles, requestId and IP from the request). Modules pass before/after as structured JSON plus short human text ('Held $1,240.00' → 'Available $1,240.00') for the list.

audit has no hard dependencies so every module can use it. It is optional for others (ctx.tryUse('audit')); if disabled, modules still work and the kernel logs a warning that material actions are not being recorded. It should stay enabled in every real deployment.

Entries are never updated. The approval column comes from approval_states, which follows access events (requested → partially approved → approved), so an entry created with 'Pending · waiting for Morgan Hale' later shows 'Approved'.

Tamper evidence: entries form a hash chain by seq; the repository only inserts entries (the database user's role should allow no update or delete on audit.entries but the purge's). Checkpoints (table checkpoints) carry an HMAC-SHA256 over seq and hash keyed with secretFor(config, 'audit.checkpoint'), a key the database never holds, so rewriting entries and recomputing every hash is still detected. Purges write a checkpoint first so verification continues across purged ranges, then delete the expired entries by their indexed at. Entries deleted behind the app's back break the chain and verify-chain reports it.

Categories: support (cases, remedies, goodwill decisions), trust (reports, recommendations, enforcements, appeals), inventory (adjustments, transfers, counts, discrepancies), shipping (labels, claims, carrier services, holidays, exceptions) join the earlier ones; modules that recorded these as other switch to their own category (old entries keep theirs).

Choosing a category (record): pick it by the kind of record and decision, not by the module that writes it. financial: money moves and money decisions (payouts, holds, adjustments, write-offs, refunds and their approval, disputes, fees, wallet credit and gift cards, supplier costs, ad charges). seller_enforcement: warnings, restrictions, suspensions, closures and performance actions taken against a seller by the sellers module. trust: what Trust and Risk does (reports, recommendations, enforcements and their reversal, appeals), even when the target is a seller. catalog: products, categories, brands, offers and prices, listing media. orders: orders, order items, cancellations and order fulfilment. returns: return requests, inspections and return decisions other than the refund money. customers: customer accounts, notes, customer conversations and data requests. support: cases, remedies and goodwill decisions. inventory: stock adjustments, transfers, counts and discrepancies (warehouse stock too). shipping: labels, shipments, carrier claims, carrier services, holidays and delivery exceptions. content: pages, help articles, policies, review moderation and notification content. advertising: campaigns, creatives, placements and ad rules. access: roles, permissions, limits, staff and seller member access, approvals and away periods. security: sign-in and step-up events, private file downloads, personal data exports, integrity alerts. settings: configuration of any module (settings changes, thresholds, routing, templates, carrier and queue settings). other: only what fits none of these. getSummary counts financial, seller_enforcement and settings for its chips.
Secrets are never stored: redactKeys are masked at record time; payout account numbers appear only as last 4 digits.
Retention 7 years is the prototype's example; the legal requirement is a business decision to confirm.

Exports: audit registers dataset audit.admin.entries with reports.registerDataset and serves the rows through exportRows; the job, file, link expiry and link logging are reports' (requestExport, getExport, listExports). reports is an optional dependency checked at call time; while it is disabled the audit Export button is hidden (DATASET_UNAVAILABLE).
